branch_hypotheses.observable_divergence_signal: Cross-channel wording becomes consistent and resident question volume falls within one tick.
branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: Schools, translators, and newsrooms converge on the same interpretation, confusion narrows, and trust stabilizes.

branch_hypotheses.trigger: Official correction appears but translated versions lag by one or more ticks.

branch_hypotheses.observable_divergence_signal: Family-reported clarity rises in school channels while citywide resident confusion remains high.

branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: Residents and media interpret the issue as institutional incompetence, reducing trust beyond the drill itself.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Original confusing map remains visible without prominent correction or is corrected ambiguously.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: This endpoint is contradicted if one or more major audiences remain dependent on conflicting interpretations at drill start.
endpoint_ledger.description: Most salient audiences receive actionable, comprehensible evacuation-zone guidance before the drill begins.
endpoint_ledger.label: Broad usable information achieved

meta.important_question: By the start of the drill, which major audiences have received usable evacuation-zone information rather than merely seeing the original map?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: The scenario explicitly asks who received usable information.
realization_criteria: Observable evidence that city_residents, school_linked_households, and language_access_reliant_households each receive a clear instruction set or corrected map before drill start.
Cross-channel reports indicate reduced ambiguity in what zone applies and what action is expected.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: T0 shows confusion with multiple possible clarification intermediaries but no confirmed broad resolution yet.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Contradicted if the original confusing map remains the most shared reference or if official clarification is too vague to replace it.
endpoint_ledger.description: A city-issued correction, replacement map, or plain-language explainer becomes the dominant reference over the initial confusing post.
endpoint_ledger.label: Official correction supersedes original

meta.important_question: Does the city issue a correction or explainer that becomes more visible than the original confusing map?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Correction visibility is central to trust and downstream comprehension.
realization_criteria: A corrected or clarifying official artifact is published and prominently linked or distributed.
Subsequent media, school, and community references predominantly point to the corrected artifact rather than the original post.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Correction pressure is explicit, but no superseding correction is yet realized at T0.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Not realized if official emergency management regains clear primacy as the trusted interpreter across audiences.
endpoint_ledger.description: An intermediary other than the original city source becomes the main trusted interpreter for key audiences.
endpoint_ledger.label: Intermediary trust capture

meta.important_question: Which actor becomes the primary trusted interpreter of the situation: city emergency management, schools, translators, or local news?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: The scenario foregrounds communication trust and reactive interpreters.
realization_criteria: Survey-like signals, engagement patterns, or repeated public references show schools, translators, or local news are relied upon more than city emergency management for understanding the map.
Resident or household behavior follows intermediary explanations even when official materials remain ambiguous.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: T0 trust is mixed and confusion creates opening for trust transfer away from the original source.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Parity and persistent gap are mutually exclusive terminal states on this axis.
endpoint_ledger.description: The system resolves either toward roughly comparable multilingual usability or a persistent information inequality by drill start.
endpoint_ledger.label: Language access parity or gap

meta.important_question: Do multilingual households receive corrected, usable information on a timeline comparable to English-dominant audiences?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: The source explicitly includes volunteer translators and asks who received usable information.
realization_criteria: Parity realized if translated/culturally usable corrections reach language-access-reliant households within the same effective decision window as general audiences.
Gap realized if multilingual households rely on delayed, inconsistent, or unofficially patched interpretation while other audiences already have stable guidance.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: T0 evidence strongly suggests language access is outcome-relevant but unresolved.

merge_hypotheses.convergence_effect: Even strained actors may align around a common explainer once ambiguity is recognized.
merge_hypotheses.mechanism: All major actors benefit from a single simple interpretation before the drill starts.

merge_hypotheses.convergence_effect: Public debate cools as institutions and intermediaries repeat the most actionable available guidance.
merge_hypotheses.mechanism: If the drill timing approaches and no new contradictory information appears, participants may settle on a practical minimum-consensus message.

merge_hypotheses.convergence_effect: Residents, schools, and translators may synchronize around media framing when official messaging is incomplete.
merge_hypotheses.mechanism: A widely shared local explainer can provide a de facto common interpretation across groups.

risk_flags.note: City size, channel mix, and institutional capacity are not specified; counts are calibrated defaults for a compact municipal scenario.
Scenario is seeded with confusion and pressure but not full crisis, preserving room for correction dynamics.
Volunteer translators are salient, but exact language distribution and official translation resources are unspecified.
High dependence on one confusing map means small design or prominence changes can produce large branch divergence.
Even strong official correction may struggle to overtake screenshots of the original map in peer channels.

core_premises: Official emergency communication contains confusing map information.
Residents, emergency managers, school officials, and volunteer translators are salient actors.
Trust, correction events, and distribution of usable information are central outcome drivers.
The scenario should remain compact and not begin at maximum crisis.
initial_uncertainty: Exact city size and media ecosystem are unspecified.
No confirmed harm event at T0; confusion risk is present but not yet fully realized.
Audience segmentation and language access gaps are implied but not quantified in source text.
simulation_brief.summary: A fictional city releases confusing evacuation-zone maps ahead of a storm drill. Communication quality, trust, correction dynamics, and unequal access to usable information are the main T0 pressures.

sociology_baseline.note: People are more likely to accept clarifications from already trusted intermediaries than from unfamiliar sources.
Public complaint or active questioning rises if confusion is repeated across channels or validated by peers/media.
Some households privately doubt comprehension but do not publicly signal confusion unless prompted by trusted community nodes.
Residents preferentially verify information within familiar language, school, or neighborhood networks.
Belief that maps are unusable or corrected usually needs reinforcement from multiple sources.
School-linked and language-community identities shape who is seen as credible.
If corrections are delayed or not salient, many low-attention residents disengage rather than resolve confusion.

sociology_prompt_influences.description: Confusing initial official visuals reduce message uptake unless accompanied by plain-language restatement.
Schools, translators, and local news can outperform the original source in perceived usability when they simplify instructions.
If corrections arrive in English first and multilingual updates lag, information inequality widens quickly.
Repeated alignment across city, school, translator, and news channels materially improves confidence in interpretation.
